=== FILE: Dockerfile ===
# Build stage: compile and run the unit tests with Maven.
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY pom.xml .
RUN mvn -q -B dependency:go-offline || true
COPY src ./src
RUN mvn -q -B package

# Runtime stage: only the JRE and the jar.
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /src/target/*.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080
USER 1000
CMD ["sh", "-c", "echo 'fund-transfer built and tested. Add a main program and update CMD in the Dockerfile.'"]

=== FILE: .dockerignore ===
.git
.github
**/node_modules
**/target
**/__pycache__
**/.pytest_cache
selenium-*/
playwright-*/
k8s/
*.md
run.json

=== FILE: scripts/build.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds, tests and packages fund-transfer as a Docker image, then runs it on port 8080.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "==> Build"
mvn -B -q -DskipTests package
echo "==> Unit tests"
mvn -B -q test
echo "==> Docker image"
docker build -t fund-transfer:latest .
echo "==> Run (Ctrl+C to stop)"
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 fund-transfer:latest

=== FILE: scripts/build.ps1 ===
# Builds, tests and packages fund-transfer as a Docker image, then runs it on port 8080 (Windows PowerShell).
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
Set-Location (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..")

Write-Host "==> Build"
mvn -B -q -DskipTests package
Write-Host "==> Unit tests"
mvn -B -q test
Write-Host "==> Docker image"
docker build -t fund-transfer:latest .
Write-Host "==> Run (Ctrl+C to stop)"
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 fund-transfer:latest

=== FILE: .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml ===
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  IMAGE: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/fund-transfer

jobs:
  build-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
      - name: Build
        run: mvn -B -q -DskipTests package
      - name: Unit tests
        run: mvn -B -q test

  docker:
    needs: build-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build (and push on main)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          tags: ${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }},${{ env.IMAGE }}:latest

  deploy:
    # Optional: set repository variable DEPLOY_ENABLED=true and secret KUBE_CONFIG (base64 kubeconfig).
    needs: docker
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && vars.DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v4
      - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.KUBE_CONFIG }}" | base64 -d > kubeconfig
          export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/kubeconfig
          kubectl apply -f k8s/
          kubectl set image deployment/fund-transfer fund-transfer=${{ env.IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          kubectl rollout status deployment/fund-transfer

=== FILE: docker-compose.yml ===
services:
  fund-transfer:
    build: .
    image: fund-transfer:latest
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - PORT=8080
    restart: unless-stopped

=== FILE: k8s/deployment.yaml ===
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fund-transfer
  labels:
    app: fund-transfer
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fund-transfer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fund-transfer
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: fund-transfer
          image: ghcr.io/OWNER/fund-transfer:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: PORT
              value: "8080"
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi

=== FILE: k8s/service.yaml ===
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: fund-transfer
spec:
  selector:
    app: fund-transfer
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP

=== FILE: DEPLOY.md ===
# Deploying fund-transfer (Java)

Generated by BOT's Deploy stage. Everything below runs from the folder that contains this file.

## 1. Build and test locally

    mvn -B -q -DskipTests package
    mvn -B -q test

Or run the whole chain with `scripts/build.sh` (Linux/macOS) or `scripts/build.ps1` (Windows).

## 2. Build the Docker image

    docker build -t fund-transfer:latest .
    docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 fund-transfer:latest

The Dockerfile is multi-stage: the first stage builds the code and runs the unit tests, so a broken build never produces an image.

> No entry point (main program) was found in the code, so the image builds and tests it and then prints a message. Add a main program or HTTP server and update the `CMD` line.

## 3. Run with Docker Compose

    docker compose up --build

## 4. CI/CD with GitHub Actions

Commit the project with `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`. On every push and pull request it builds, runs the unit tests and builds the Docker image. On `main` it also pushes the image to the GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io/<owner>/fund-transfer`).

The optional `deploy` job runs only when the repository variable `DEPLOY_ENABLED` is `true` and the secret `KUBE_CONFIG` holds a base64-encoded kubeconfig.

## 5. Kubernetes

    kubectl apply -f k8s/
    kubectl rollout status deployment/fund-transfer
    kubectl port-forward service/fund-transfer 8080:80

Edit the `image:` line in `k8s/deployment.yaml` to point at your registry first.

# Feature: Fund Transfer Between Accounts

## Story 1: Transfer Funds Between Accounts
As a <bank employee>, I want to transfer funds between accounts, so that I can manage my finances more effectively.

### Acceptance Criteria
Scenario: Transfer funds between accounts
  Given I have an account with a balance of $1000
  When I initiate a transfer to another account with a balance of $500
  Then the balance of my account should be $500
  And the balance of the receiving account should be $1500
  And an audit log should be created with the transfer details

## Story 2: Transfer Funds Between Accounts with Error Handling
As a <bank employee>, I want to handle errors during fund transfers, so that I can prevent fraud and ensure the integrity of the system.

### Acceptance Criteria
Scenario: Transfer funds between accounts with error handling
  Given I have an account with a balance of $1000
  When I initiate a transfer to another account with a balance of $500
  And the receiving account does not have enough funds
  Then an error message should be displayed
  And the balance of my account should remain $1000
  And the balance of the receiving account should remain $1000
  And an audit log should not be created

## Story 3: Transfer Funds Between Accounts with Audit Trail
As a <bank employee>, I want to keep track of all fund transfers, so that I can audit the system and ensure compliance with regulations.

### Acceptance Criteria
Scenario: Transfer funds between accounts with audit trail
  Given I have an account with a balance of $1000
  When I initiate a transfer to another account with a balance of $500
  Then an audit log should be created with the transfer details
  And the balance of my account should be $500
  And the balance of the receiving account should be $1500
  And the audit log should be updated with the transfer details

## Assumptions
- The bank has a secure and reliable system for managing account balances and transactions.
- The bank has a robust audit trail system to track all transactions.
- The bank has a system for managing user roles and permissions.
- The bank has a system for handling errors during transactions.
